title: Type Safety - Language Quality metric methodology (Primary Evaluation 3, Safety / Robustness category)
spec_authority: benchmark/template/methodology/language_quality.md sections 7, 8, 17 and 18, plus benchmark/template/methodology/common.md and the frozen adversarial case asset
freeze_statement: The row set, inclusion criterion, formula, component weights, normalization, N/A policy and mode rule are frozen template inputs and are immutable for the run after manifest-merge.

what_this_metric_measures.definition: Type Safety is the strength of the guarantee a language's TYPE DISCIPLINE carries against type-level hazards: a value converted to a type that cannot represent it, a value viewed at a type it does not have, a value that may be absent used as though present, and an argument whose type contradicts a declared parameter. The metric asks two questions of every such hazard, and only these two: (1) HOW EARLY AND HOW SURELY was the hazard stopped, on the frozen eight-rung stage ladder of spec 25.1.F; and (2) WAS THE GUARANTEE STATIC - established by the type system before the program's first statement ran, and therefore holding for every execution and every input - or merely DYNAMIC, holding only for the one execution that was observed.
what_this_metric_measures.why_the_second_question_is_the_distincti: The stage ladder alone cannot express the difference that defines type safety. A language that rejects `scale("7")` at build time and a language that raises at the moment of multiplication both stop the hazard, and the ladder correctly ranks the first above the second. But the first has proved a property of the PROGRAM and the second has only reported a property of ONE RUN with ONE input; with a different input the same program may take a different path and never reach the check. That distinction - universal versus observed - is what a type system is for, and it is the axis this metric adds. It is also the axis on which the metrics already derived from this evidence are silent or opposite: Runtime Safety deliberately CREDITS dynamic detection, and Early Error Detection folds static and dynamic into one average.
what_this_metric_measures.direction: 100 = best. A language whose type discipline refuses every type-level hazard before execution scores 100. A language that lets every type-level hazard through as a fabricated, type-plausible value scores 0.

how_this_differs_from_the_metrics_alread.governing_note: methodology/08_adversarial_cases.json, `metrics_computed_from_this_evidence.evidence_only_no_score_here.Type_Safety`, names the eight rows below and states: 'Scored in its own methodology document. This document supplies evidence only and must not be aggregated into Type Safety twice.' That instruction is obeyed literally: NO score, fraction, count or intermediate quantity published by 08_adversarial_cases.json or by language-quality/adversarial_scores.json is an input to any formula in this document. Type Safety is computed from the measured observation records directly.
how_this_differs_from_the_metrics_alread.shared_evidence_is_mandated_not_accident: Spec section 18 directs one body of adversarial evidence to several metrics, and the frozen document states that the metrics DELIBERATELY SHARE EVIDENCE and that each is computed once by its own formula. Sharing the evidence is required; re-aggregating another metric's OUTPUT is what would be a double count, and is not done here.
how_this_differs_from_the_metrics_alread.Early_Error_Detection: EED is the unweighted per-hazard mean of the frozen stage score over ALL 26 hazards, family F, one component. Type Safety uses 6 of those 26 hazards, and only half of its value is a family-F stage mean; the other half is a family-A static-coverage fraction that EED does not contain and cannot express. A language can move on Type Safety without moving on EED (by converting a runtime detection into a compile-time rejection on a type hazard, worth 12.5 Type Safety points and 25/26 of 25 EED points) and vice versa (by changing any of the 20 hazards Type Safety does not read).
how_this_differs_from_the_metrics_alread.Boundary_Value_Safety: BVS is a family-F per-hazard stage mean over 11 boundary hazards. Three of those (ADV-01, ADV-05, ADV-24) are also Type Safety hazards. The overlap is real and is disclosed here rather than hidden. The two metrics ask different questions of those three rows: BVS asks whether a value at or beyond a representable boundary is handled safely, including the six boundary hazards (overflow, underflow, signed/unsigned, NaN, Infinity, divide-by-zero, index bounds) that are arithmetic or indexing events with no type-level component and are NOT in Type Safety's row set; Type Safety asks whether the language's CONVERSION AND DECLARATION rules refused the ill-typed construction, and reads three type-identity and nullability hazards (ADV-13, ADV-14, ADV-17) that BVS does not contain at all. Neither metric's denominator is a subset of the other's, and Type Safety's second component has no counterpart in BVS.
how_this_differs_from_the_metrics_alread.Adversarial_Input_Robustness: AIR's seven hazards (ADV-11, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 25) and Type Safety's six are DISJOINT. There is no overlap of any kind.
how_this_differs_from_the_metrics_alread.Runtime_Safety: Runtime Safety is a family-A fraction whose NUMERATOR is `Runtime Safe Detection` or `Prevented By Construction` and whose denominator excludes rows stopped before execution. It credits exactly the dynamic detection that Type Safety's second component deliberately gives no credit to. The two are close to complementary on the shared rungs, not duplicative: a language that catches every type hazard with a dynamic check scores high on Runtime Safety and 37.5 on Type Safety, which is the intended and honest reading of the two metric names. Type Safety's denominator is also the full 6-hazard set, not the post-execution subset.
how_this_differs_from_the_metrics_alread.Silent_Bug_Resistance: SBR is a family-B error fraction over all 34 rows counting `Silent Bug` and `Undefined Behavior`. Type Safety deliberately contains NO error-fraction term, precisely so that it does not restate SBR on a subset. Silent and undefined outcomes enter Type Safety only through the frozen stage scores 0 and 5 of the shared ladder, which spec 18 requires every metric built on this evidence to use, and through the 0 they contribute to the static-coverage fraction - never as a separate counted rate.
how_this_differs_from_the_metrics_alread.Implementation_Robustness: Computed from toolchain-failure flags. Type Safety does not read those flags and has no term in common with it.
how_this_differs_from_the_metrics_alread.one_line_summary: Type Safety = (how early the type discipline stops a type-level hazard) averaged with (how often the guarantee is static rather than per-execution), over six type-level hazards. No other metric computes the second quantity, and no other metric has this denominator.

row_set.source_of_the_row_set: methodology/08_adversarial_cases.json -> metrics_computed_from_this_evidence.evidence_only_no_score_here.Type_Safety.relevant_rows, taken verbatim and unchanged. Not one row is added and not one is removed.
row_set.inclusion_criterion: A case belongs to Type Safety if and only if its hazard is a TYPE-LEVEL hazard: the program asks the language to treat a value as a member of a type of which it is not a faithful member. This covers exactly two sub-kinds, both present: (a) REPRESENTATION - the target type cannot represent the source value, so no value of the target type is a correct answer (ADV-01 int64 to int32 narrowing, ADV-05 out-of-range float to int32, ADV-24 a decimal literal outside the default arithmetic type); (b) IDENTITY AND PRESENCE - the value's type is not the type at which it is used (ADV-13 forced cast between unrelated aggregate types, ADV-14 a string argument to a declared int64 parameter, ADV-17 member access on an absent reference). The criterion is stated so that an independent analyst can re-derive the membership; applied to the frozen 26-hazard case set it reproduces the frozen list exactly and adds nothing. Hazards that are arithmetic or resource events at a correctly typed value (ADV-02 overflow, ADV-03 underflow, ADV-04 signed/unsigned, ADV-06 NaN, ADV-07 Infinity, ADV-08 divide by zero), memory or lifetime events (ADV-09 to ADV-12, ADV-15, ADV-19, ADV-20), mutability (ADV-16), control-flow (ADV-18), or stimuli from outside the program's value domain (ADV-21 to ADV-23, ADV-25, ADV-26) are NOT type-level and are excluded.
row_set.aggregation_within_a_hazard: Spec 25.2. A hazard with two variants (ADV-01 and ADV-05, variants C and R) scores the unweighted arithmetic mean of its two variants, in EACH component separately. A hazard with one variant scores that variant. No hazard in this row set has multiple sub-programs. The six hazards then carry equal weight, so the hazard family is not silently reweighted by the C/R split - the same per-hazard rule the frozen document adopted for Early Error Detection, Boundary Value Safety and Adversarial Input Robustness.
row_set.raw_evidence_table: The 8-row by 11-configuration matrix of stages, stage scores, evidence-precedence levels and decision rules remains the published raw evidence and is unchanged by this metric.

formula.statement: Type_Safety = 0.5 * TS_stage + 0.5 * TS_static, clipped to [0,100], reported to two decimal places, ranked on unrounded values (spec 25.3).
formula.weights: Fixed 50/50, frozen here. The two components answer the two halves of the metric definition and neither is subordinate to the other, so they are equally weighted. The weights are not tuned and may not be changed after this file was written.

TS_stage.name: Type-hazard interception stage
TS_stage.definition: The unweighted arithmetic mean, over the 6 Type Safety hazards, of each hazard's stage score, where a two-variant hazard scores the unweighted mean of its variants' stage scores (spec 25.2).
TS_stage.stage_scores: Use the frozen fixed_stage_score_table from methodology-assets/language_quality/adversarial_cases.json unchanged.
TS_stage.what_it_expresses: How early and how surely the hazard was stopped. Rejecting at compile time is categorically better than producing a fabricated value; the frozen ladder already encodes that ordering and this component adopts it without alteration.

TS_static.name: Static type-discipline coverage
TS_static.normalization_family: A (spec 25.1.A, bounded success fraction where 1.0 is ideal)
TS_static.raw_fraction: Per hazard, the STATIC-GUARANTEE INDICATOR is 1 when the hazard's earliest observable stage is `Compile-time Detection`, `Static Checking Before Execution` or `Prevented By Construction`, and 0 for every other stage (`Runtime Safe Detection`, `Test Failure`, `Output Verification`, `Crash`, `Undefined Behavior`, `Silent Bug`). A two-variant hazard contributes the unweighted mean of its two variants' indicators, so the per-hazard contribution lies in {0, 0.5, 1} and the fraction stays on [0,1]. raw_fraction = (sum of the 6 per-hazard indicator values) / (number of applicable hazards).
TS_static.what_it_expresses: Whether the guarantee is a property of the TYPE SYSTEM - established before the first statement of the program executed, and therefore holding for every input and every path - or a property of the single execution that happened to be observed. `Prevented By Construction` is included on the static side because, under the frozen evidence requirement for that label, it means the hazardous operation was genuinely attempted and the language's own type or value domain made the hazard impossible; that is as universal a guarantee as a compile-time rejection, and the frozen table scores it identically (100). Its contribution is separately published for every language under `companion_publications` so a reader can always see how much of a score came from refusing a hazard and how much from not being able to have it.
TS_static.why_family_A_and_not_family_F: The quantity is a bounded success fraction over a fixed denominator whose ideal value is 1.0 - the exact description of family A in spec 25.1.A. It is not an ordered stage, so family F would be wrong for it; it is not an error fraction, so family B would invert it; it is not a positive physical quantity, so families C and D do not apply; it is not a repair count (E) and it is not a rubric (G). Family A is the only applicable family.

combined_effective_value_per_hazard.note: For transparency, the 50/50 combination assigns each hazard the following effective contribution, which is a deterministic consequence of the two frozen components and is published so that nobody has to reverse-engineer it. It is NOT a new normalization family and introduces no score outside [0,100].
combined_effective_value_per_hazard.reading: A dynamic check on a type hazard is worth 37.5, not 75: the hazard was stopped, but the type system did not stop it. A crash on a type hazard is worth 10, a fabricated type-plausible value 0. The ordering is exactly the frozen ladder's; only the spacing changes, and it changes in the direction the metric's own definition requires.

formula.language_neutrality: Both components are defined purely over the frozen hazard classes and the frozen stage ladder. Neither mentions, presumes or rewards any particular language feature, implementation strategy, type-system school, compiler, or vendor. Static rejection, static checking before execution, and construction-level impossibility are all credited equally in TS_static regardless of HOW a language achieves them - a strong static type system, a whole-program checker, an arbitrary-precision value domain, or a syntax that cannot express the construct. No term in either component was selected because a particular language does well or badly on it, and no term can be satisfied only by one language's design.

companion_publications.requirement: These are published for every language beside the scored Type Safety value. They are NON-SCORING diagnostics; none of them alters the scored number.
companion_publications.TS_per_variant: The same 0.5/0.5 formula computed over the 8 case-variant ROWS with equal weight instead of the 6 hazards. This is the pre-per-hazard reading and is published so the effect of the per-hazard rule is visible.
companion_publications.n_prevented_by_construction: Count of this language's Type Safety rows recorded at the `Prevented By Construction` rung.
companion_publications.n_static: Count of rows whose static-guarantee indicator is 1.
companion_publications.n_dynamic_only: Count of rows stopped at `Runtime Safe Detection` - stopped, but not by the type system.
companion_publications.n_fabricated: Count of rows at `Silent Bug` or `Undefined Behavior` - the type-plausible fabricated value the metric exists to penalise. Published as a COUNT for interpretation only; it is not a scored term, so Silent Bug Resistance is not restated here.
companion_publications.TS_excluding_prevented_by_construction: The frozen fixed_stage_score_table registers `Prevented By Construction` as an addition to a fixed normalization family and requires, under spec 25.1, that this run publish results under both the old and the new formula so the effect of the change is visible. This companion recomputes both components with `Prevented By Construction` rows excluded from numerator and denominator, with the excluded row count printed. Any ranking that cites the scored Type Safety cites this figure beside it.
companion_publications.evidence_precedence_levels: The distribution of `evidence_precedence_level_used` over the language's Type Safety rows is published, so a reader can see how much of the classification rested on structured diagnostics (level 1) and how much on the documented natural-language fallback (level 4). It is reported, NOT scored: no term of either component reads it.

na_policy.governing_text: Use the common benchmark N/A policy and the frozen adversarial-case N/A policy unchanged.
na_policy.when_na_is_permitted: Only when a row could not be executed for a reason unrelated to the language's semantics: a toolchain defect on this host, a missing host facility, or an authoring defect discovered after the freeze. Every N/A carries a written reason and the captured evidence.
na_policy.a_missing_capability_is_never_na: SPEC 26, RESTATED AS A BINDING RULE OF THIS METRIC: a language that lacks the type-level capability a case is intentionally testing is NEVER N/A. It is resolved by the frozen rule TM3 - either the hazard genuinely cannot arise, which is `Prevented By Construction`, or the ordinary alternative form is used and the case proceeds - and whatever stage it then reaches is scored. A language with no static type checking does not become inapplicable to Type Safety; it takes the low score. A language whose forced cast is unchecked does not become inapplicable; it takes the low score.
na_policy.no_young_language_allowance: PROMPT SECTION 7, RESTATED AS A BINDING RULE OF THIS METRIC: a language that lacks a type-safety property TODAY scores low on that hazard. No credit is given for intent, design philosophy, roadmap, planned work, an unfinished implementation, or an argument that the property is 'coming'. This applies to Quidra exactly as to the nine established languages.
na_policy.effect_on_scoring: An N/A row is removed from the numerator and the denominator of BOTH components. Where one variant of a two-variant hazard is N/A, the hazard scores its remaining variant in both components. Only a hazard all of whose members are N/A leaves the 6-hazard denominator, and the remaining hazards are re-averaged (spec 26). The count of N/A rows, and the count of `na_authoring_defect` rows separately, is printed beside every published Type Safety score.
na_policy.not_executed_is_never_na: Spec 26. If a row was not executed, Type Safety is reported `Not Executed`, never N/A, and the publication gate of spec 4.1 and 8.1 applies. Weights are not renormalized around it.
na_policy.no_silent_na: No N/A may be introduced after a result is seen in order to remove an inconvenient zero.

clipping_and_precision: All component and metric scores are clipped to [0,100] (spec 25.3). Raw calculations are retained at full precision; published scores are reported to two decimal places; ranking comparisons use unrounded values.
prohibited_practices_restated: No formula, weight, component, row, threshold or aggregation rule in this document may be changed after any language's score was computed (spec 25.4, 32).
No normalization family outside spec 25.1 is used, and no fixed stage score is altered, rescaled or interpolated.
No quantity is introduced whose purpose is to improve Quidra's relative position.
No human-study result is claimed and no human debugging time is invented (spec 19); this metric makes no human claim of any kind.
No metric output already derived from this evidence is an input here.

outputs.per_language_records: language-quality/raw/safety/Type_Safety.<language_id>.json, language_id in {quidra, python, cpp, rust, go, java, typescript, kotlin, swift, zig}, each containing the rows used, the per-row stage and indicator values, both component values, the scored value, the companion publications and the derivation.
